problems.title: The location formatter repeats the row as the column
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, p. 8; Appendix C.4, p. 25; certain_key_all_location lines 200–221.
claim: The all-occurrences generator stores row/column pairs correctly but formats both output coordinates using the row component.
analysis: In a two-by-three table with target cells \((1,2)\) and \((2,3)\), the stored pairs are correct but the output is \((1,1),(2,2)\). Neither formatted cell need contain the target.
result: This generator can produce wrong answer coordinates. Its final training-data linkage is not established.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Format row from the first stored component and column from the second, preserving the structured pair until serialization.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local data-generation error without a demonstrated central benchmark effect.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Ragged rows can silently lose columns
claim: The Markdown serializer derives column widths from a transpose before making every row equally long.
analysis: For rows \([H_1,H_2]\) and \([r_1,r_2,\mathrm{LOST}]\), `zip(*rows)` exposes only two columns. The resulting format has no third placeholder, so the extra cell disappears. Pre-padding and some repeated-call paths avoid this boundary.
result: The serializer does not preserve every cell of arbitrary ragged input. A blanket claim about all generated prompts is not warranted.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Copy and pad every row to the maximum width before deriving widths and placeholders, then serialize all columns without mutating the original table.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a conditional serializer defect, not evidence that every prompt was truncated.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Some fixed-size assets have inconsistent actual widths
problems.source_location: Section 3.3/Figure 4, pp. 6–7; Tables 7–8, pp. 26–27; NIAT_cropped_tables.json records 0,12,29,37.
claim: The public fixed-size JSON and corresponding prompts are presented as equal-dimension long-table inputs.
analysis: Among fifty inspected records, advertised \(28\)-by-\(28\) cases at indices \(0,12,37\) store \(28\)-by-\(32\) arrays and expose those extra columns in their prompts. Record \(29\) instead stores width \(29\) but serializes width \(28\); it is not another extra-column prompt.
result: The assets need a shape/provenance correction before a fixed-size analysis. The entire Figure 4 result is not numerically refuted.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Align dimension metadata, stored arrays and the actual serialized prompt for each affected asset. Use original predictions and experiment mapping before revising any aggregate metric.
problems.impact_rationale: The discrepancy affects a few released records; their exact contribution to the central experiment is unestablished.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
